issue_context.title: AIP-84 Migrate the public endpoint Get Task to FastAPI
issue_context.body:
### Description

Currently the Get Task public endpoint is at `api_connexion/endpoints/task_endpoint.py` under `get_task`. We need to migrate it to the `api_fastapi/views/public/tasks.py` under a `get_task` or similar.

Features and functionality of the endpoint will remain unchanged.

### Use case/motivation

AIP-84 cWiki Link: https://cwiki.apache.org/confluence/display/AIRFLOW/AIP-84+UI+REST+API

### Related issues

Related to: https://github.com/apache/airflow/issues/42370

review_comments: Calling sync method (making network/IO requests) from async function? Doesn't this block the event loop?

FastAPI knows how to run sync code from default async routes. For now all the API code is sync because we are missing some async utility code in airflow core.

This will be changed in the future when we have time to tackle that.

> FastAPI knows how to run sync code from default async routes

That's not true. There is no special magic under the hood of FastAPI. It just wraps all sync endpoints (`def`) into `asyncio.to_thread`, sending them to ThreadPool, and not blocking the current event loop. For `async def` endpoints, it does not do that. If `async def` endpoint calls blocking sync method, the entire event loop will block.

True, I got confused, I thought It was run in an external threadpool, but that's only  true for `non async` route.I think we need to remove all of the `async` keyword as long as the code has blocking sync operations.

I'll open a PR for that, thanks for pointing it.

PR is ready here, https://github.com/apache/airflow/pull/43797

Thanks again.

> Calling sync method (making network/IO requests) from async function? Doesn't this block the event loop?

Thanks for highlighting this @dolfinus! Yes the sync func will block the event loop for that particular thread. We can probably explore and consider making the sync funcs async, and then can call those async ones from the async path funcs. Please see [this comment](https://github.com/apache/airflow/pull/43797#issuecomment-2463876083).

i think sooner than later we should probably try to add the basic nuts and bolts for asyncio so we can make use of it.

since we're doing all this work migrating code to new thing that supports asyncio, why not just make it async.

https://github.com/apache/airflow/pull/43940

so, it seems not too impossible
